thread:
maya: Heads-up — canary shows a memory/perf weirdness after today's runtime merge. Hosts serving longctx (>=2048) see OOMs during warmup and repeated eviction spikes. filing here before I escalate to incidents.

jonathan: seen it too on a2-prod-5. OOMs start ~30s after load spike, fragmentation + eviction rate goes up. Rolling back didn't repro. perf-bot CI flagged a +12% p95 token latency too. :frowning:

ranjit: curious if this is eviction policy change or kernel switch from the routing refactor. On my local repro I saw a lot of small allocations around KV slab headers during warmup.

sasha: repro script I ran (short seqlen sweep) shows eviction oscillation whenever sequence length crosses 1024 -> 2048 boundary. dump attached below (shortened):

```
[2026-03-17T14:02:10Z] kv_evict: window=128 free=12 used=1016
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] kv_evict: evict_count=72 reclaimed=18 frag_ratio=0.42
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] kv_evict: window=256 free=6 used=2046
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] oom: alloc failed for slab 3 size=4096
```

jonathan: interesting — kernel router change (commit 6a1b2f7) added a fallback that chooses a different cuda kernel for >1024 tokens. Could be causing allocation alignment differences.

ranjit: started git bisect. First bad commit narrowed to range: 6a1b2f7..7c9d1aa. Bisect result points at 7a3e5c2 — the batching heuristics change (dynamic batch packing) that interacts with fastpath KV allocation.

maya: perf traces (summary): when dynamic packing enabled we get more short-lived KV fragments; `perf top` shows hotspots in kv_map::insert and slab_split. stack snippet:

```
# perf top sample
  12.1% kv_map::insert
   9.3% slab_alloc_fastpath
   7.8% kernel_select::choose_fast
```

sasha: I also profiled with PPC (page compaction counters) — page churn spikes during the first 45s of traffic with dynamic packing on. Reproduce steps attached in gist: https://internal/gists/kv-warmup-repro

perf-bot: CI perf suite: nightly-longctx-2048 failed on p95 latency (12% regression) and mem pressure alert. Job: runners/longctx/2048. Link: https://ci.internal/longctx/2176

jonathan: temporary mitigation ideas:
- force kernel selection to legacy path for >1024 in canary
- disable dynamic batch packing (rollout flag)
- tune kv eviction warmup to be more conservative (increase grace window)

ranjit: quick local test: disabling dynamic packing + reverting kernel fallback removes oscillation. So interaction seems non-linear; maybe dynamic packing creates denser short-lived prefixes and kernel fallback changes allocation alignment.

maya: agree. Proposal: hold canary rollout, flip dynamic packing off in canary, and do a focused bisect that includes the kernel-fallback and packing changes together. Also bump eviction grace window from 5s->20s as a stopgap.

eng-sre: holding rollout and pinned canary to previous build. I've added an alert to block any auto-rollout until eng-runtime gives :white_check_mark:.

sasha: I'll open a focused PR that isolates packing change for review + add a KV warmup test in CI that runs a seqlen sweep to catch this. Also adding a perf regression test for p95 on longctx.

maya: thanks. tagging @security and @product for visibility since this affects Hosted SLAs. Next steps: (1) revert packer for canary, (2) increase eviction warmup, (3) run extended bisect with perf traces, (4) decide on targeted revert vs fix. Update here when bisect narrows commit list.

jonathan: bisect follow-up: added perf traces for 7a3e5c2..7c9d1aa and saw that enabling only kernel-fallback (without packing) doesn't trigger OOMs. So packing change is the proximate cause; kernel-fallback amplifies it. I'll draft a revert of packing and a cleaner implementation that avoids small-slab churn.

maya: perfect. If anyone finds additional repro signals (page compaction counters, slab histogram) drop them here. Thanks folks :thumbsup:
